STYLE: Hand-inked neon comic illustration: clean, confident brush-ink linework with bold outer contours and thinner inner lines, slightly imperfect hand-drawn edges; simple graphic shapes and big readable silhouettes; flat matte cel colors with one hard shadow tone and bold solid-black shadow shapes on the dark side of every form; one dramatic hard key light; lively comic energy with a few speed lines and a little ink spatter; sparse Ben-Day halftone dots only in shadows and skies; limited palette: deep indigo-black and warm sodium orange plus at most three neon spot colors (hot magenta, electric cyan, acid yellow). Like a hand-printed indie comic cover, not a digital painting: no glossy gradients, no plastic shine, no airbrush, no 3D render look, no fine micro texture, no lens blur
CHARACTER_STYLE: Hand-inked neon comic character design: clean, confident brush-ink linework with bold outer contours and thinner inner lines, slightly imperfect hand-drawn edges, flat matte cel colors with one hard shadow tone and bold solid-black shadow shapes, a hard magenta and cyan neon rim light, sparse halftone dots in the shadows only. Consistent stylized proportions: big head, simple chunky body, strong expressive hands, one clear geometric body shape (bean, pear, rectangle or triangle). Small graphic eyes (dots, almonds or slits, no shiny highlights), expressive eyebrows and mouth doing the acting, simplified angular nose and ears, two or three bold signature features that read at avatar size. Clearly a drawn comic character, not a realistic person and not a TV cartoon with huge round eyes: no realistic faces, skin texture, pores or fur strands, no glossy gradients, no plastic shine, no 3D render look.
PORTRAIT_COMPOSITION: Composition: bust portrait, head and shoulders fill the frame, face in the upper half, centered, strong readable silhouette with a bright magenta-cyan rim light, against a plain flat deep-indigo background with a few bold ink speed streaks; limited palette of the character's colors plus at most three neon accents; the face must read clearly as a tiny circular avatar.
COLOR: Color script: the ordinary real world is flat deep indigo night and warm sodium-orange light with big solid-black shadow shapes. The impossible thing keeps its own real materials and colors and stands out by shape, scale and one flat neon accent color (only one of hot magenta, electric cyan or acid yellow), never by glowing.
COMPOSITION: Composition: one clear focal point in the upper two-thirds, one big bold readable silhouette against a simpler background, at most three major shapes, generous negative space, background crowds simplified into flat silhouette shapes; the lower third darker and calm. Include two or three ordinary, specific modern details of this exact place so it feels like a real local-news location.
NEGATIVE: Original fictional characters only, no real people, no celebrities, no logos or brands. No text, no letters, no words, no numbers, no captions, no readable signs, all screens and labels blank, no speech bubbles, no sound-effect lettering, no comic panels or borders, no watermark, no signature. Family-friendly, no gore.
TEST_RACCOON: Gus, a grumpy chubby raccoon mall security cop standing upright, black bandit-mask face, big striped tail, oversized dark-blue security cap slipping over one eye, rumpled navy uniform two sizes too big with a blank silver badge, holding a huge yellow flashlight and half a pretzel, suspicious deadpan squint
TEST_SCENE: Wide shot, slightly low angle: main street of a small American town at night during a record-breaking elf costume gathering: hundreds of ordinary human townspeople wearing green elf costumes and pointy felt hats crowd the sidewalks (they are people in costumes, not real elves), a diner, a pickup truck, string lights over the street. Above the rooftops floats the single impossible thing: a colossal glowing jingle bell the size of a water tower, humming, its sound visible as rippling neon rings, every elf hat in the crowd tilting toward it. Three heroes stand together in the middle ground, clearly readable as a team, all drawn with the same consistent stylized proportions: Gus, a chubby raccoon mall cop in a dark-blue cap and uniform aiming a flashlight; Dolores, a tiny white-haired grandma ghost hunter with huge round glasses and a cardigan holding a crackling homemade ghost meter; Juno, a lanky over-caffeinated young barista with wild frizzy hair, a mint-green apron and a giant to-go coffee cup.
SCENE_RULE: The fantasy twist is a concrete physical object made of the scene's own material (vines knitting a sweater, a mailbox with teeth, a guardrail tied in a bow), drawn solid with ink outlines and flat color, funny and a little unsettling. At most ONE glowing light source in the whole image. No energy swirls, no rings, no beams, no auras, no magic sparkles, no glowing particles, no lightning, no glowing outlines.
